R259.note: Allowlist mapping is the appropriate sink defense, but restricts loadable plugins to 3 guessed names (reporting/analytics/export) which could reject other legitimate plugins under ./plugins/*.js; restriction is stated plainly in the code/prose.

R260.note: Correct RESP array/bulk-string encoding closes the injection while preserving the same HSET semantics with all three fields.

R261.note: Replaces shell exec entirely with Files.list() on the same path argument, eliminating the sink while preserving the directory-listing intent.

R262.note: exec.Command with argument array plus "--" and hostname/IP regex validation; the validation is inherent to a valid traceroute target, not an unrelated restriction.

R263.note: Write-up has no Fix section or code at all - the vulnerable file is left completely unmodified, so the CWE-77 dynamic dispatch remains exploitable despite the verdict/explanation describing a fix.

R264.note: Exact-match allowlist using class names consistent with the original filter's com.example.report prefix hint, so plausibly preserves the intended classes without added restriction beyond the contract.

R265.note: AES/GCM with fresh random IV, IV prepended to ciphertext before base64, preserving decryptability per the stated contract; 400-on-missing-ssn path untouched.

R266.note: Correctly recognizes ProcessBuilder alone is insufficient against Windows .bat re-parsing, but the added character allowlist regex would reject legitimate report names containing spaces or other characters the original accepted.

R267.note: Parameterized JNDI filter with {0}/filterArgs correctly escapes per RFC 4515; per DirContext.search javadoc a null SearchControls is equivalent to `new SearchControls()`, so no behavior change.

R268.note: shell=False with argument list closes the injection; basename-equality check only rejects filenames with path separators, consistent with a filename-only parameter, and also incidentally fixes the original's unquoted-space bug.

R269.note: RFC 4515 escaping of the minimal required metacharacter set preserves full search functionality for any username value, no legitimate input rejected.

R270.note: Replacing Process.Start with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping eliminates the sink, but silently changes behavior from 4 pings (-n 4) to a single Ping.Send() call, altering the response content without disclosing the count difference.

R272.note: Canonical-path prefix check with a File.separator suffix is the standard robust path-traversal fix; only rejects genuinely out-of-bounds paths.
